note: REVIEWED MANUAL EDIT 2026-08-13 — X evidence retired at the site owner's instruction ("remove all references to x posts and stop using the x api for the predictions"). peterTotal (30), peterAuthored (11) and maxReuse (9) were floors on @peterxing X posts. The evidence they measured no longer exists, so they are removed here rather than zeroed: a floor of 0 would read as a satisfied gate, and leaving them at 30/11/9 would fail closed forever by design. This removal is the reviewed manual path this file prescribes for lowering a value, and the matching automatic writer in refresh-signals.js is retired in the same change so no builder-computed value can reach this file. The ratchet MECHANISM is unchanged and still guards the currency registrations below; nothing was loosened to make a run pass. Monotonic ratchet semantics continue to apply to every remaining key.
currencyLedgerSourcesNote: Count of reviewed sources in the currency ledger. AGE DEMOTION NEVER SHRINKS THE LEDGER — it removes a link from signals.json while the reviewed source remains — so this floor is unaffected by a demotion and a drop below it means a source was DELETED, not demoted. Every currency consistency check compares the page against the ledger, so when both shrink together they agree and the loss is invisible; this is the only pin on the reference itself. Raising it is a reviewed manual edit.
currencyMaxAgeDaysNote: EXACT REGISTRATION, not a ratchet. The ceiling the currency demotion is SUPPOSED to use. The artefact records what governed publication and the environment records what a machine thinks today, but BOTH resolve from CURRENCY_MAX_AGE_DAYS, so a single deploy-config edit moves both and they agree at the wrong value. This is the only term in the comparison that the thing under test cannot rewrite. That is a checked property, not an assumed one: refresh-signals.js DOES write this file on a ratchet advance, and it used to emit only its own three fields and delete every registration beside them, so this value would have vanished at the next Peter improvement. That writer now preserves what it does not own and asserts its own key set. Friday's numerator exists only because 60 demotes one source; at 90 nothing demotes and every gate still passes. REVISED 2026-08-13 from 60 to 14 at the site owner's instruction ("references based on the latest news from the last 2 weeks"). SEMANTICS STATED EXPLICITLY: the implemented rule is unchanged and is Math.round(ageDays) > currencyMaxAgeDays, so demotion fires at 14.5 days, NOT at 14.0. This is a registration of the ceiling actually implemented, not of the one the instruction reads as. Measured before the change: absoluteAge rejected 4 of 125,042 candidate pairings, so this ceiling is not what limits coverage; the subject matcher is.
currencyLedgerIdentitiesNote: EXACT REGISTRATION of WHICH ten sources are the reviewed ones, not how many. currencyLedgerSources is a CARDINALITY and a cardinality cannot see a SUBSTITUTION: replace a reviewed source with a never-reviewed one, hold the count at 10 and hold publishedAt constant, and every page/ledger check agrees because both sides moved together — measured, exit 70 with zero findings, while the traceability line still reported 11 of 11 links resolving to a reviewed entry. Host is not fine enough either: these 10 sources span only 6 hosts, so 3 spectrum.ieee.org entries are mutually substitutable under a host assertion. Identity is the finest grain there is, which is why the regress stops at the full URL. publishedAt is registered with it because Friday BUILDS ITS PREDICTED DEMOTION INSTANT FROM IT (publishedAt + ceiling), and the only other check on that field compares the page against the ledger, which one coherent edit moves together. Changing any entry is a reviewed manual edit made here.
